intro: Talking about your job, job interviews, the working day, meetings, holidays and deadlines. Use *Sie* in interviews and with clients; colleagues often say *du*, especially in Switzerland and in younger companies. In Switzerland 'holidays' are usually *Ferien*, not *Urlaub*.

phrases.en: What do you do for a living?
phrases.usage: A common small-talk question. Answer *Ich bin Ingenieurin.* or *Ich arbeite als ...* With *du*: *Was machst du beruflich?*
phrases.grammar: *beruflich* is an adverb ('professionally'). In the answer, a profession after *sein* has no article: *Ich bin Lehrer.* (not ✗ *ein Lehrer*).

phrases.en: I work as a software developer.
phrases.usage: The answer to *Was machen Sie beruflich?* A woman says *Software-Entwicklerin*. To name the employer use *bei*: *Ich arbeite bei einer Bank.*
phrases.grammar: *als* + profession without article; the noun is in the same case as the subject (Nominativ). The usual spelling is one word, *Softwareentwickler*; the hyphen is also allowed for readability.

phrases.en: I have a job interview tomorrow.
phrases.usage: Tell friends or family. They usually answer *Viel Erfolg!* or *Ich drücke dir die Daumen!* ('I'll keep my fingers crossed').
phrases.grammar: The time adverb *morgen* stands in the Mittelfeld before the object. Compound with linking *-s-*: *die Vorstellung* + *s* + *das Gespräch* → neuter → *ein Vorstellungsgespräch* (Akkusativ).

alternatives.de: Ich bin morgen zu einem Vorstellungsgespräch eingeladen.
alternatives.en: I've been invited to a job interview tomorrow.
Tomorrow I have a job interview.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a new position.
phrases.usage: Tell people in your network. Job ads are called *Stellenangebote* (in Switzerland also *Stelleninserate*).
phrases.grammar: *suchen* + Akkusativ. *die Stelle* is feminine → *eine*. After *eine* in the feminine Akkusativ the adjective takes **-e**: eine neu**e** Stelle.

phrases.de: Wie lange arbeiten Sie schon hier?
phrases.en: How long have you been working here?
phrases.usage: Small talk with a new colleague or at a company event. The answer is *Seit zwei Jahren.* or *Erst seit März.*
phrases.grammar: German uses the Präsens + *schon* for an action that started in the past and is still going on; English needs the present perfect continuous. Do not use the Perfekt here (✗ *Wie lange haben Sie hier gearbeitet?* asks about a finished period).

alternatives.en: Since when have you been working here?

alternatives.de: Wie lange bist du schon in der Firma?
alternatives.en: How long have you been with the company?

phrases.en: My workday starts at nine.
phrases.usage: Describe your routine, for example in small talk or in an exam conversation about daily life. Many offices in Switzerland have flexible hours (*Gleitzeit*).
phrases.grammar: *um* + clock time. *beginnen* is a strong verb: *begann, hat begonnen*. Compound: *die Arbeit* + *s* + *der Tag* → *der Arbeitstag*, so *mein*.

alternatives.de: Ich arbeite von neun bis sechs.
alternatives.en: I work from nine to six.

phrases.en: I work from home.
phrases.usage: Very common now. In companies people also say *Ich bin heute im Homeoffice.* or *Ich mache Homeoffice.* (in German *Homeoffice* means working from home).
phrases.grammar: Fixed phrase *von zu Hause* (often *von zu Hause aus*). *zu Hause* ('at home') is written as two words; *zuhause* is also allowed. *Hause* is an old Dativ form that survives only in these phrases.

alternatives.de: Ich arbeite heute von zu Hause aus.

phrases.en: We have a meeting today.
phrases.usage: *das Meeting* is common in international companies. More German words: *die Besprechung* and, very common in Switzerland, *die Sitzung*.
phrases.grammar: Loan words from English are often neuter: *das Meeting* → Akkusativ *ein Meeting*. *heute* stands before the object in the Mittelfeld.

alternatives.de: Heute ist um zehn eine Sitzung.
alternatives.en: There's a meeting at ten today.

phrases.en: Can we reschedule the meeting?
phrases.usage: Ask a colleague or client politely; add the reason and a proposal. The answer is *Ja, wann passt es Ihnen?*
phrases.grammar: *verschieben* means 'move to another time' (earlier or later); the new time follows with *auf* + Akkusativ: *auf Donnerstag verschieben*. Inseparable prefix *ver-* → Partizip *verschoben*. *der Termin* → Akkusativ *den*.

alternatives.de: Können wir den Termin auf Donnerstag verschieben?
alternatives.en: Can we move the meeting to Thursday?

alternatives.de: Passt Ihnen auch ein anderer Tag?

phrases.en: I need vacation.
phrases.usage: A sigh after a busy time. To your boss: *Ich möchte Urlaub beantragen.* In Switzerland people usually say *Ferien*: *Ich brauche Ferien.*
phrases.grammar: *der Urlaub* is uncountable here, so there is no article. Common combinations: *Urlaub nehmen*, *im Urlaub sein*, *in den Urlaub fahren*.

alternatives.de: Ich möchte nächste Woche Urlaub nehmen.
alternatives.en: I'd like to take leave next week.

phrases.en: My boss is very friendly.
phrases.usage: Talk about your workplace. A female boss is *die Chefin*. In formal texts the word is *der/die Vorgesetzte*.
phrases.grammar: *freundlich* is predicative after *sein*, so it has no ending. *der Chef* is a normal masculine noun (*den Chef, dem Chef*).

alternatives.de: Ich verstehe mich gut mit meinem Chef.
alternatives.en: I get on well with my boss.

phrases.en: I have a lot to do.
phrases.usage: A polite reason to keep a conversation short or to say no to an extra task. The other person may answer *Dann will ich nicht länger stören.*
phrases.grammar: *haben* + *zu* + infinitive means 'to have something to do'. *viel* has no ending here. Compare *Ich habe nichts zu tun.*

alternatives.en: I've got a lot of work at the moment.

phrases.en: The deadline is tomorrow.
phrases.usage: Spoken office German. Strictly, *die Frist* is the period, so more exact forms are *Die Frist endet morgen.* or *Der Abgabetermin ist morgen.* In many companies people simply say *die Deadline*.
phrases.grammar: *sein* + time adverb (*morgen*). With a verb of ending: *Die Frist läuft morgen ab.* (separable *ablaufen*).

phrases.en: I have to write an email.
phrases.usage: In Germany it is *die E-Mail*; in Switzerland and Austria many people say *das E-Mail*. In speech the short form *Mail* is common.
phrases.grammar: *müssen* + infinitive at the end. With feminine *die E-Mail* the Akkusativ is *eine E-Mail* (Swiss neuter: *ein E-Mail*).

alternatives.de: Ich schreibe dir später eine E-Mail.
alternatives.en: I'll write you an email later.

alternatives.de: Ich muss noch eine Mail beantworten.
alternatives.en: I still have to answer an email.

phrases.en: Have a nice evening (after work)!
phrases.usage: Said to colleagues when you or they leave work. The answer is *Danke, dir auch!* or *Gleichfalls!* *Feierabend machen* means 'to finish work for the day'.
phrases.grammar: Akkusativ wish without article: *der Feierabend* is masculine → *schönen*.

alternatives.en: See you tomorrow, have a nice evening!

words.en: end of the working day, time after work

phrases.de: Ich bin heute krank und komme nicht ins Büro.
phrases.en: I'm sick today and won't come to the office.
phrases.usage: Call or write to your boss early in the morning. In Switzerland your contract or the company rules say from which day you need an *Arztzeugnis*; in Germany you need a doctor's note if you are ill for more than three days, and the employer can ask for it earlier.
phrases.grammar: Two main clauses joined with *und*; the subject *ich* is not repeated, so there is no comma. *ins* = *in das*: *in* + Akkusativ for a direction.

alternatives.de: Ich kann heute leider nicht arbeiten, ich bin krank.
alternatives.en: I'm afraid I can't work today, I'm sick.

phrases.de: Ich bin nächste Woche im Urlaub.
phrases.en: I'm on holiday next week.
phrases.usage: Tell colleagues and clients in advance, and set up an automatic email reply. In Switzerland: *Ich bin nächste Woche in den Ferien.*
phrases.grammar: *im Urlaub* = *in dem Urlaub*, Dativ (a state, not a direction). *nächste Woche* is a time expression in the Akkusativ without preposition (*die Woche* → *nächste*).

alternatives.de: Ich bin nächste Woche in den Ferien.

alternatives.en: I have time off next week.

phrases.de: Könnten Sie mir das bitte erklären?
phrases.en: Could you explain that to me, please?
phrases.usage: Ask your boss or a colleague when a task or a term is not clear. It is normal to ask; people usually answer *Ja, natürlich.* and explain.
phrases.grammar: *könnten* is the Konjunktiv II of *können* and makes the request more polite than *können*. *erklären* takes a Dativ person (*mir*) and an Akkusativ thing (*das*).

alternatives.de: Kannst du mir kurz zeigen, wie das geht?
alternatives.en: Can you quickly show me how it works?

phrases.de: Ich schicke Ihnen die Unterlagen bis Freitag.
phrases.en: I'll send you the documents by Friday.
phrases.usage: A typical promise in emails and meetings. *bis Freitag* means 'by Friday at the latest'. The other person answers *Perfekt, danke.*
phrases.grammar: German uses the Präsens for a future promise. Dativ person (*Ihnen*) before the Akkusativ noun (*die Unterlagen*). With two pronouns the Akkusativ comes first: Ich schicke **sie Ihnen** bis Freitag.

alternatives.de: Sie bekommen die Unterlagen bis Freitag.
alternatives.en: You'll get the documents by Friday.
I'll send them to you tomorrow.

phrases.en: Are you coming to lunch with us?
phrases.usage: Invite a colleague you say *du* to. The answer is *Gern, ich komme gleich.* or *Heute leider nicht, ich habe zu viel zu tun.*
phrases.grammar: *mitkommen* is separable, and *mit* closes the Satzklammer. The phrase *zum Mittagessen* is placed after it (Ausklammerung), which is normal in speech. *zum* = *zu dem* (Dativ), *das Mittagessen*.

alternatives.en: Shall we go and eat together?

phrases.de: Ich bin für dieses Projekt verantwortlich.
phrases.en: I'm responsible for this project.
phrases.usage: Explain your role in a meeting, an interview or an email. In an interview you may continue with *Ich leite ein Team von fünf Personen.*
phrases.grammar: *verantwortlich für* + Akkusativ: *das Projekt* is neuter → *dieses Projekt*. The adjective *verantwortlich* stands at the end, after *sein*.

alternatives.de: Das Projekt liegt in meiner Verantwortung.
